name: Sculptor
introduction: is the Sculptor’s Workshop, introduced by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 1750s. It is a faint constellation in the southern sky near Fomalhaut.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: The south pole of our galaxy lies in Sculptor: looking here, we look straight out of the Milky Way’s disk into intergalactic space.
The Sculptor Galaxy, NGC 253, is one of the brightest galaxies in the sky and a starburst galaxy, forming new stars at a high rate.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alpha Sculptoris](hip:4577) is a blue-white giant about 700 light-years away. [Beta Sculptoris](hip:116231) and [Gamma Sculptoris](hip:115102) complete the figure.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Sculptor also contains the Sculptor Dwarf, a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, and the Cartwheel Galaxy, a ring galaxy formed by a collision.
